title: Numbered security invariants, and a security-reviewer agent (PI-02)
summary: Also known as PI-02. The four 'Security rules (hard constraints)' sat inside the BACKEND-DEV section of CLAUDE.md, so FRONTEND-DEV and ISSUE-FIXER never read them despite both routinely touching tenant-data paths. No verification steps, no severities, and no security agent in the 13-agent roster on a multi-tenant platform running two untrusted embedded runtimes (Lua, Wasm) for tenant-authored scripts. Tenant-isolation-critical requirements (FIL-06, QRY-04, SBX-05, CAC-UI-01, DDL-05) shipped reviewed by nobody.

design_decision.invariant_count: Started from the six invariants given verbatim in docs/agents/PIPELINE_BACKLOG.md PI-02 (INV-1 tenant data isolation, INV-2 server-side field authorisation, INV-3 untrusted-runtime sandboxing, INV-4 secrets by reference, INV-5 not-found/forbidden indistinguishability, INV-6 new-path proof-of-scoping). Kept all six unchanged in substance. Added two more (INV-7 no SQL string interpolation, INV-8 no catch unreachable on realistic failure paths) rather than silently dropping them: both were among the four rules previously stated only in CLAUDE.md's BACKEND-DEV section ('Security rules (hard constraints)'), and folding them into the numbered scheme was the explicit alternative offered by the task brief to letting them disappear. The other two of the original four rules were folded into existing invariants rather than given new numbers: 'no secrets in source' merged into INV-4 (config secrets and tenant secrets are the same rule applied to two populations), and 'no I/O in src/engine/transition.zig' was kept as project-wide guidance directly in CLAUDE.md rather than promoted to a numbered invariant, since it is a single-file purity constraint rather than a tenant-security boundary (already enforced by the pre-existing 'transition.zig in-file tests' CI job). Final count: 8 invariants, all BLOCKER severity — no MAJOR/MINOR tier for cross-tenant exposure or secret leakage on this platform.
design_decision.codebase_grounding: Each invariant's Reference section cites the actual enforcing/related code: INV-1 -> src/api/tenant_context.zig, src/db/pool.zig (schemaNameForTenant, per-connection search_path), src/db/provisioning.zig, tests/integration/tnt_schema_isolation_test.zig (TNT-01..04), tools/lint_migration_schema.py's 21-table BUSINESS_TABLES enumeration; discovered mid-investigation that this platform's tenant scoping is schema-per-tenant (search_path), not a tenant_id row predicate as PI-02's own INV-1 wording implied -- the Rule text was adjusted to state this precisely rather than copy the backlog wording verbatim, since the wrong mental model (row predicate vs. schema isolation) would misdirect SECURITY-REVIEWER's actual checks. INV-3 -> src/lua/capabilities.zig (CapabilitySet), src/wasm/capabilities.zig (StandardCapabilities + wildcard matching), src/lua/host_api/, src/wasm/host_api/. INV-4 -> src/secrets/{reference,store,redaction,crypto}.zig, the sec:// reference scheme, ISS-0074/GH-289 (the plaintext-secret-storage incident that motivated src/secrets/ existing). INV-5 -> FIL-06/SBX-05 in docs/requirements.yaml, tests/simulation/scenarios/platform/platform-{attachment,sandbox}-cross-tenant-probe.yaml (existing UAT scenarios already encode this exact BLOCKER expectation). Every 'How to verify' command was run for real before being written down, not guessed: zig build test-lua, zig build test-crypto-iss0074, zig build test-misc-unit all confirmed exit 0; zig build test-integration-tnt confirmed 'Build Summary: 8/8 steps succeeded; 34/34 tests passed' against a live BPM_TEST_DB_URL. Several invariants (INV-2, INV-5, INV-7 interpolation-specifically, INV-8) are honestly marked '(manual -- no automated check yet)' rather than citing a linter that doesn't actually check that property.
design_decision.agent_placement: SECURITY-REVIEWER modelled directly on CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's file (also a gate/validator role, not an implementer) for frontmatter format, tone, and structure. Inserted into CLAUDE.md's WF-02 step table as Step 2c, after 2a/2b (BACKEND-DEV/FRONTEND-DEV implementation) and before Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER), matching the issue's own wording exactly. Given a scope test (does the diff touch a tenant-data path?) so it never blocks non-tenant-data changes -- an unconditional gate on every WF-02 run would be disproportionate to Effort:M and would slow down unrelated work for no security benefit. Also updated docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md's flow diagram and added a full Step 2c section, matching Step 1b's level of detail, so the two step-table sources (CLAUDE.md summary table, the detailed workflow doc) don't diverge.
design_decision.ci_gate: Checked first whether any existing CI job already ran cross-tenant isolation tests: confirmed .github/workflows/ci.yml has exactly one workflow, and its only database-backed job (fresh_database_migration) runs zig build migrate against a fresh Postgres service but never runs zig build test-integration-tnt or any other integration test -- the 'build' job is explicitly no-database by its own header comment. So the 'Done when' CI criterion was genuinely unmet, not already satisfied. Added a new tenant_isolation_tests job mirroring fresh_database_migration's existing pattern (ephemeral postgres:15 service, migrate then test), scoped to zig build test-integration-tnt specifically (TNT-01..04) since that requires only Postgres (no Keycloak) and is the direct runtime check for INV-1. Runs on every push/PR to main (no path filter narrower than the workflow's own trigger), which covers 'any change under src/' as a superset rather than a narrower path-filtered subset.
design_decision.not_done: Did not touch .github/agents/*.agent.md or .github/instructions/*.md (the Copilot-harness parallel surfaces) -- the issue scope named .claude/agents/ specifically, and tools/lint_agent_docs.py does not require parity across the three surfaces, only internal consistency within whichever files exist. Did not add a dedicated interpolation-specific SQL linter, a field-authorisation linter, or a not-found/forbidden byte-equality integration test -- each of those gaps is stated explicitly in security-invariants.md as '(manual -- no automated check yet)' rather than silently built or silently left unstated; building all of them would exceed Effort:M for this issue.

resolution: 1) docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md (new): eight numbered invariants (INV-1..INV-8), each with Rule / Reference / How to verify / Severity, plus a coverage note explaining the two additions beyond the six given in the backlog. 2) .claude/agents/security-reviewer.md (new): SECURITY-REVIEWER agent definition modelled on code-design-validator.md's structure. 3) CLAUDE.md: WF-02 step table gained Step 2c (SECURITY-REVIEWER, hard gate for in-scope changes); new '## AGENT: SECURITY-REVIEWER' section added between CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR; BACKEND-DEV's 'Security rules (hard constraints)' section replaced with a pointer to the new invariants file plus a short summary (no diverging duplicate copy). 4) docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md: SECURITY-REVIEWER added to the agent roster table and the capability matrix. 5) docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md: flow diagram updated with a Step 2c box; Step 2a/2b next_action lines updated to route through Step 2c; new 'Step 2c -- Security Gate' section added matching Step 1b's detail level. 6) .github/workflows/ci.yml: new tenant_isolation_tests job (ephemeral Postgres service, zig build migrate then zig build test-integration-tnt) runs the TNT-01..04 cross-tenant schema-isolation tests on every push/PR to main -- previously these tests only ran on a developer's own database and never gated a PR. 7) docs/issues/ISS-0077.json (this file).
prevention: When a security/compliance rule is stated only inside one agent's section of a shared instructions file, check which other agents actually touch the same surface (here: FRONTEND-DEV renders API responses shaped by the rule; ISSUE-FIXER diagnoses production defects that are frequently instances of the exact bug class the rule guards against) before assuming the rule's placement matches its actual audience. When extracting rules into a new canonical location, grep the old location for every rule that lived there before writing the new file, rather than working only from a backlog summary that may itself have already dropped something -- the backlog's six invariants did not mention the two pre-existing BACKEND-DEV rules (SQL interpolation, catch unreachable) at all, and they would have silently disappeared if the new file had been written purely from the backlog text. When a 'Done when' criterion says a CI job should run some category of test, verify what CI currently runs by reading the actual workflow file rather than assuming a green build implies coverage -- this repo's only integration-test-capable job (fresh_database_migration) runs migrations but no test binary at all, which was not obvious from the job's name.
